links.comparator_used: Strictly zero-shot NormWear applied to PPG without any local training or labels (also NormWear with a locally trained classifier, and unsupervised PCA features)
links.outcome: CVD detection from wearable PPG (AUROC, average precision)
links.effect: Frozen PaPaGei embeddings plus a locally trained calibrated Random Forest: AUROC 0.769, AP 0.489, recall 1.000. Zero-shot NormWear: AUROC 0.560, AP 0.226 (abstract reports 0.610 and 0.226). NormWear zero-shot with a supervised classifier: AUROC 0.667, AP 0.322. PCA features: AUROC 0.689, AP 0.208.
links.tradeoff: Needs local labels to train the classifier, though not encoder fine-tuning. The comparison is confounded by different models (PPG-specific PaPaGei vs ECG-pretrained NormWear) and different preprocessing, so the authors call NormWear a lower bound and not a fair head-to-head. Only 13 CVD cases, so results are tentative and need validation.
links.quote: Our zero-shot baseline (NormWear, AUROC 0.560) represents truly label-free deployment but yields insufficient discrimination, highlighting that some local labels substantially improve utility.

design_hint: local classifier training on frozen embeddings vs zero-shot use
